items.stem: A new agent loops overnight and drives API spend up. The team shares one organization across three projects. The team needs a monthly ceiling for each project and a stop for a single runaway loop.
options: Set a monthly spend limit on each project workspace with alerts, and cap tool calls per run in code.
Raise the workspace rate limit, so the loop finishes its work within the same hour.
Set a spend limit on the Default Workspace that holds the project key.
Create a separate organization for each project, each with its own billing and dashboard.
items.rationale: A workspace spend limit caps monthly spend for each project, and alerts fire at thresholds that you choose. A call cap in code stops one runaway run within minutes. (Inference)
items.trap: A higher rate limit looks like a fix for a stalled loop, but it allows more calls and raises spend.

items.stem: An audited workflow calls an alias for an earlier model. The output must stay fixed through a validation period. The team must also find any deprecated use before the retirement date.
options: Keep the alias, since aliases for earlier models point to a fixed snapshot that never moves.
Move the workflow to the newest model now, and skip the replacement test to save time.
Pin a dated snapshot ID, and export usage by key and model to find deprecated use.
Build a shadow environment that replays every request to two model IDs, with a dashboard per token.
items.rationale: A dated snapshot ID stays fixed for the validation period. A usage export by key and model shows which calls still use deprecated models.
items.trap: An alias for an earlier model sounds fixed, but it points to the most recent snapshot for that minor version.

items.stem: An assistant summarizes a long contract, and a wrong claim has a real cost. The model must stay the same. Each claim must point to source text. Which two controls meet these constraints?
options: Use a larger model tier for summaries, because larger tiers invent fewer contract terms.
Ask for word-for-word quotes before the summary, because the contract is a long document.
Turn on contract mode, which blocks any summary that lacks a citation.
Remove each summary claim that has no source quote, after the quote check runs.
items.rationale: Quotes before the summary ground each claim in the text of the document. Claims with no quote are removed, so each claim that stays in the summary is checkable.
items.trap: A larger model tier looks like the fix for invented terms, but the constraints keep the same model.
